1	/**
2	 * pi-ai assistant event translation into the Harness streaming protocol.
3	 *
4	 * pi-ai tool-call arguments are parsed objects while the Harness keeps their
5	 * raw JSON representation. pi-ai also reports failures as terminal stream
6	 * events, which this module maps into Harness finish chunks.
7	 *
8	 * @module dsh-llm-pi-ai/stream
9	 */
10	
11	import { brandString } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-brand'
12	import { CONTEXT_WINDOW_EXCEEDED_CODE, EMPTY_RESPONSE_CODE, isContextWindowExceededError, isQuotaExceededError, LlmError, QUOTA_EXCEEDED_CODE } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm'
13	import type { FinishReason, StreamChunk, TokenUsage, ToolCallId } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm'
14	import { isContextOverflow } from '@earendil-works/pi-ai'
15	import type { AssistantMessage, AssistantMessageEvent, Usage as PiUsage } from '@earendil-works/pi-ai'
16	import { toPiReplayState } from './replay.ts'
17	
18	/**
19	 * Map pi-ai usage (reasoning folded into output by pi-ai).
20	 * @param usage - cumulative usage from the terminal pi-ai event.
21	 * @returns harness counts with pi-ai's exact total; cache fields appear only
22	 *   when non-zero (pi-ai reports zeros, not absence).
23	 */
24	export function mapUsage(usage: PiUsage): TokenUsage {
25	  return {
26	    inputTokens: usage.input,
27	    outputTokens: usage.output,
28	    totalTokens: usage.totalTokens,
29	    ...usage.cacheRead > 0 ? { cacheReadTokens: usage.cacheRead } : {},
30	    ...usage.cacheWrite > 0 ? { cacheWriteTokens: usage.cacheWrite } : {},
31	  }
32	}
33	
34	// XXX(pi-ai upstream): pi-ai flattens the caught error to `error.message`
35	// (api/anthropic-messages.js: `errorMessage = error instanceof Error ?
36	// error.message : JSON.stringify(error)`), discarding the original Error and its
37	// `cause` chain before it reaches us. undici carries the actionable transport
38	// detail on `cause` (e.g. `SocketError: other side closed`) but hands the fetch
39	// wrapper a bare `terminated`, so we are left pattern-matching terse words here.
40	// If pi-ai ever forwards the original Error (or a fetch/dispatcher hook that lets
41	// us capture the cause ourselves), classify on `code`/`cause` instead of text.
42	// The first standalone 4xx/5xx number is the status. Digits inside addresses
43	// and ports are not: OmniRoute reports a `[502]: fetch failed` whose cause lists
44	// IPv6 addresses such as `2001:4860:4844:400::`, and that 400 is not the status.
45	function httpStatus(message: string): number | undefined {
46	  const match = /(?<![\w.:/-])[45]\d\d(?![\w.])/.exec(message)
47	  return match === null ? undefined : Number(match[0])
48	}
49	
50	function classifyPiAiError(message: string): string {
51	  const status = httpStatus(message)
52	  if (status === 401 || status === 403) return 'AUTH'
53	  if (isQuotaExceededError(message)) return QUOTA_EXCEEDED_CODE
54	  // Gateways such as OmniRoute report a brief credential cooldown without a
55	  // status code: `All credentials for model … are cooling down (reset after 5s)`.
56	  if (status === 429 || /rate.?limit|cooling down/i.test(message)) return 'RATE_LIMIT'
57	  // A rejected request body (gateway or provider size cap): resending the
58	  // same request cannot succeed, so it is invalid, not transient.
59	  if (status === 413 || /failed to buffer the request body:\s*length limit exceeded|payload too large|request body too large/i.test(message)) return 'INVALID_REQUEST'
60	  if (status === 400 || /invalid.?request/i.test(message)) return 'INVALID_REQUEST'
61	  if (status !== undefined && status >= 500) return 'SERVER'
62	  if (/\btime(?:d)?\s*out\b|timeout/i.test(message)) return 'TIMEOUT'
63	  // A stream truncated before the provider's terminal event: each pi-ai provider
64	  // throws its own wording when the wire closes mid-response without a terminal
65	  // event (`… stream ended before message_stop`, `… before a terminal response
66	  // event`, `… ended without a terminal event`, `Stream ended without
67	  // finish_reason`). The connection dropped mid-response, so this is a transport
68	  // truncation, not a model-level error.
69	  if (/stream ended (?:before|without)\b/i.test(message)) return 'TRANSPORT'
70	  if (/\b(?:network|connection|socket|fetch)\b|\bECONN[A-Z]+\b/i.test(message)
71	    || /\b(?:other side closed|HTTP2 request did not get a response|WebSocket closed unexpectedly)\b/i.test(message)
72	    // undici renders a mid-stream socket drop as a bare `terminated` (its
73	    // `cause` — the real SocketError — was flattened away upstream); Node's
74	    // stream layer says `Premature close`.
75	    || /\bterminated\b|premature close/i.test(message)) {
76	    return 'TRANSPORT'
77	  }
78	  return 'PI_AI_ERROR'
79	}
80	
81	/**
82	 * Map a terminal pi-ai event to the harness finish reason.
83	 * @param message - the assistant message carried by the `done` or `error` event.
84	 * @param contextWindow - resolved catalog capacity for usage-based overflow detection.
85	 * @returns the mapped harness reason. Recognized error text, `stop` usage above
86	 *   `contextWindow`, and zero-output `length` usage that fills the window map
87	 *   to `CONTEXT_WINDOW_EXCEEDED`; a `stop` with no content blocks maps to an
88	 *   `EMPTY_RESPONSE` error, while terminal `pending` and `deferred` states map
89	 *   to non-retryable `PI_AI_ERROR` failures.
90	 */
91	export function mapStopReason(message: AssistantMessage, contextWindow?: number): FinishReason {
92	  const piAiOverflow = isContextOverflow(message, contextWindow)
93	  const harnessOverflow = message.stopReason === 'error'
94	    && message.errorMessage !== undefined
95	    && isContextWindowExceededError(message.errorMessage)
96	  if (piAiOverflow || harnessOverflow) {
97	    return {
98	      kind: 'error',
99	      failure: {
100	        message: message.errorMessage ?? `pi-ai detected context overflow for model "${message.model}"`,
101	        code: CONTEXT_WINDOW_EXCEEDED_CODE,
102	      },
103	    }
104	  }
105	
106	  switch (message.stopReason) {
107	    case 'stop':
108	      // A terminal stop that produced no content blocks is a degenerate
109	      // provider completion, not a successful (empty) assistant message.
110	      if (message.content.length === 0) {
111	        return {
112	          kind: 'error',
113	          failure: {
114	            message: `model "${message.model}" returned a completed response with no content`,
115	            code: EMPTY_RESPONSE_CODE,
116	          },
117	        }
118	      }
119	      return { kind: 'stop' }
120	    case 'length': return { kind: 'max-tokens' }
121	    case 'toolUse': return { kind: 'tool-calls' }
122	    case 'pending': return {
123	      kind: 'error',
124	      failure: { message: `pi-ai stream for model "${message.model}" ended pending`, code: 'PI_AI_ERROR' },
125	    }
126	    case 'deferred': return {
127	      kind: 'error',
128	      failure: { message: `pi-ai deferred response for model "${message.model}" is not supported`, code: 'PI_AI_ERROR' },
129	    }
130	    case 'aborted': return {
131	      kind: 'aborted',
132	      failure: { message: message.errorMessage ?? 'pi-ai stream aborted', code: 'ABORTED' },
133	    }
134	    case 'error': {
135	      const text = message.errorMessage ?? 'pi-ai stream error'
136	      return { kind: 'error', failure: { message: text, code: classifyPiAiError(text) } }
137	    }
138	  }
139	}
140	
141	/**
142	 * Translate the pi-ai event stream into StreamChunks. pi-ai never throws
143	 * mid-stream — failures arrive as `error` events, which become error/aborted
144	 * `finish` chunks (the harness protocol's other error-delivery style).
145	 * @param events - one assistant turn's pi-ai event stream.
146	 * @param contextWindow - resolved catalog capacity for usage-based overflow detection.
147	 * @param callerSignal - caller cancellation state; an aborted caller makes any
148	 *   in-band terminal error an aborted finish.
149	 * @returns the harness chunks, ending with `usage` then `finish`; throws
150	 *   `LlmError` (`STREAM_CLOSED`) if the source ends without a terminal event.
151	 */
152	export async function* toStreamChunks(
153	  events: AsyncIterable<AssistantMessageEvent>,
154	  contextWindow?: number,
155	  callerSignal?: AbortSignal,
156	): AsyncGenerator<StreamChunk> {
157	  // pi-ai contentIndex ↔ our block index map 1:1 (both count blocks from 0
158	  // in stream order), but we track ids per index for tool calls.
159	  const toolIds = new Map<number, { id: string; name: string }>()
160	
161	  for await (const event of events) {
162	    switch (event.type) {
163	      case 'start':
164	        break
165	      case 'text_start':
166	        yield { type: 'block-start', index: event.contentIndex, blockType: 'text' }
167	        break
168	      case 'text_delta':
169	        yield { type: 'text-delta', index: event.contentIndex, text: event.delta }
170	        break
171	      case 'text_end':
172	        yield { type: 'block-end', index: event.contentIndex, block: { type: 'text', text: event.content } }
173	        break
174	      case 'thinking_start':
175	        yield { type: 'block-start', index: event.contentIndex, blockType: 'reasoning' }
176	        break
177	      case 'thinking_delta':
178	        yield { type: 'reasoning-delta', index: event.contentIndex, text: event.delta }
179	        break
180	      case 'thinking_end':
181	        yield { type: 'block-end', index: event.contentIndex, block: { type: 'reasoning', text: event.content } }
182	        break
183	      case 'toolcall_start': {
184	        // The id/name live on the partial's content at this index.
185	        const partial = event.partial.content[event.contentIndex]
186	        const id = partial?.type === 'toolCall' ? partial.id : ''
187	        const name = partial?.type === 'toolCall' ? partial.name : ''
188	        toolIds.set(event.contentIndex, { id, name })
189	        yield { type: 'block-start', index: event.contentIndex, blockType: 'tool-call' }
190	        break
191	      }
192	      case 'toolcall_delta': {
193	        const known = toolIds.get(event.contentIndex)
194	        yield {
195	          type: 'tool-call-delta',
196	          index: event.contentIndex,
197	          id: brandString<ToolCallId>(known?.id ?? ''),
198	          ...known?.name !== undefined && known.name.length > 0 ? { name: known.name } : {},
199	          argumentsDelta: event.delta,
200	        }
201	        break
202	      }
203	      case 'toolcall_end':
204	        yield {
205	          type: 'block-end',
206	          index: event.contentIndex,
207	          block: {
208	            type: 'tool-call',
209	            id: brandString<ToolCallId>(event.toolCall.id),
210	            name: event.toolCall.name,
211	            // pi-ai hands back the PARSED arguments; the harness vocabulary
212	            // keeps the raw string.
213	            arguments: JSON.stringify(event.toolCall.arguments),
214	          },
215	        }
216	        break
217	      case 'done':
218	        yield { type: 'usage', usage: mapUsage(event.message.usage) }
219	        yield {
220	          type: 'finish',
221	          reason: mapStopReason(event.message, contextWindow),
222	          replayState: toPiReplayState(event.message),
223	        }
224	        return
225	      case 'error':
226	        // In-stream error delivery (pi-ai's style) → error finish chunk
227	        // (the harness's other sanctioned error path besides throwing).
228	        yield { type: 'usage', usage: mapUsage(event.error.usage) }
229	        yield {
230	          type: 'finish',
231	          reason: mapStopReason(
232	            callerSignal?.aborted ? { ...event.error, stopReason: 'aborted' } : event.error,
233	            contextWindow,
234	          ),
235	        }
236	        return
237	      // no default: AssistantMessageEvent is pi-ai's closed union; a new
238	      // event type should fail compilation here via tsc's exhaustiveness
239	      // when one is added (switch covers all current variants).
240	    }
241	  }
242	  throw new LlmError('pi-ai event stream ended without done/error', 'STREAM_CLOSED')
243	}

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>\n\n<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>\n\n<?claude block s1?>\n\n<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.
